post_details: Hiya, the most recent post on this subject was 10mths ago MD on the new MAC operation system Has any updates been made since? I'm currently using an M1X 32GB Macbook pro and the simulations run very poor even with a Particle distance of 20 and no AA Any help on this subject would be greatly appreciated, as this is the 1st project on this machine and it's currently a roadblock :( thx ~t
post_description: This web page aims to provide updates and support for users experiencing performance issues with simulations on M1X MacBook Pro devices.

comments.comment_body: Hello Belgrave, In response to your inquiry, please note that Marvelous Designer does not work with Apple M1 native, but work with Rosetta base that is provided by Apple. That being said, low performance or compatibility issue are highly likely expected with Apple M1. We are currently progressing to make compatibility with Apple M1, but there is yet no specific date determined for deployment of this compatibility. We will make an announcement regarding this update either via our website or the patch note when it happens. If you need further assistance or have any questions in the meantime, please do not hesitate to contact us at support@marvelousdesigner.com Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

post_details: Hi, On the last frame of my animation, the right hand of the avatar is very close to the body. So the fabric tears. Is there a way to avoid tearing of the fabric in this situation ? In DazStudio, we can deactivate a part of the body so that it is not taken into account by the simulation. Does this option exist in Marvelous ?
post_description: This web page aims to provide solutions for preventing fabric tearing in animations by exploring options within Marvelous Designer, similar to those available in DazStudio.

comments.comment_body: Hi Christina, Unfortunately, we don't have the option to deactivate part of the avatar at the moment. You can try decreasing the skin offset by selecting the avatar, then go to Property Editor. Under Surface decrease skin Offset number. You can also try increasing scene time warp before recording the simulation to reduce the speed of Animation frames. Remember to set the scene time warp back to 1 before exporting. If it's a custom animation brought into Marvelous Designer, you can create a proxy geometry for the hand. Since individual figures are not important in this simulation, you can create a proxy geometry of the outline of the hand and constraint it to the hand joint. You can also use blend shape to carve away some skin on the waist area to make more space for the garment. In addition, in Marvelous Designer we do allow user to export the Animated Avatar. You can export the avatar with animation as Alembic cache by checking "Include Avatar Shape", and tweak it using your 3D software. Best regards, Marvelous Designer Support Team

post_details: I cannot resize my workspace. It is taller than my screen. I cannot access menu items or use the program, it is in some full-screen mode with low resolution. This persists even after I restart the program. How do I reset the screen to a windowed mode?
